overview: Chad is a large landlocked country in north-central Africa, named after Lake Chad. Its capital and largest city is N'Djamena. Chad became independent from France in 1960. Arabic and French are its official languages, and it is home to more than 100 ethnic groups.

geography.text: Northern Chad is part of the Sahara and contains the Tibesti Mountains, with their volcanic peaks. The centre is the dry Sahel, and the south is wetter savanna, where most people live. Lake Chad in the west has shrunk greatly since the 1960s.

subsections.title: Climate
subsections.text: Desert in the north, savanna in the south.

subsections.title: Wildlife
subsections.text: Zakouma National Park has elephants and the rare Kordofan giraffe.

history.text: The Kanem-Bornu Empire ruled around Lake Chad for about a thousand years. France colonised the region in the early 1900s, and Chad became independent in 1960. Civil wars and conflict with Libya followed. Oil exports began in 2003, and the Déby family has ruled since 1990.

events.title: Kanem Empire
events.text: The Kanem Empire rises near Lake Chad.

events.title: Battle of Kousséri
events.text: French forces defeat the warlord Rabih az-Zubayr.

events.title: Toyota War
events.text: Chad drives Libyan forces out of the north.

events.title: Oil exports
events.text: Chad begins exporting oil through Cameroon.

government.text: Chad is a presidential republic. Idriss Déby ruled from 1990 until he was killed in 2021; his son Mahamat Déby took over and won an election in 2024. The army is very powerful.

economy.text: Oil is Chad's main export, along with cotton, cattle and gum arabic. It is one of the poorest countries in the world.

culture.text: Chad has more than 200 ethnic groups; French and Arabic are official languages. Lake Chad, once one of Africa's largest lakes, has shrunk dramatically. The Ennedi plateau has spectacular rock arches and ancient paintings.

items.title: Ennedi Massif
items.text: Sandstone arches and rock art, listed by UNESCO.

subsections.title: Food
subsections.text: Boule, a thick millet porridge with sauces.

subsections.title: Music and arts
subsections.text: Rock art in the Ennedi and Tibesti mountains.

subsections.title: Traditions and festivals
subsections.text: The Gerewol festival of the Wodaabe takes place in the Sahel.

sport.text: Football and basketball are the most popular sports. Traditional wrestling is also widely enjoyed.

items.title: Wrestling
items.text: A traditional sport across the Sahel.

didYouKnow: Lake Chad has shrunk by about 90% since the 1960s.
The Ennedi plateau has natural rock arches and rock paintings thousands of years old.

keyPeople.name: Toumaï
keyPeople.text: A 7-million-year-old skull found in Chad, among the oldest known human relatives.
